sentences.text: Pre-operative multi-sequence MRI: axial T1, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce), T2 and FLAIR, co-registered, skull-stripped and resampled to 1 mm isotropic (BraTS preparation).
The tumour contains a necrotic / non-enhancing core (confidence 0.81).
The whole-tumour mass is bilateral (confidence 0.55). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
An enhancing tumour component is present (confidence 0.97).
Whole-tumour burden is assessed as large (volume tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.99).
The enhancing fraction of the whole tumour is high (ET/WT tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.98).
Acquisition quality (cjv, efc, snr, sharpness, inu, contrast, entropy) is mildly outside the training cohort range (mean |z| = 0.77); interpret borderline findings with corresponding caution.
T1 and T1ce show a large, enhancing lesion with a central area of low signal intensity on T1 and high signal intensity on T1ce, consistent with a mass effect on the surrounding brain tissue.
The lesion shows a characteristic enhancement pattern, with a central area of high signal intensity on T1 and T1ce, and a peripheral area of low signal intensity on T2 and FLAIR.
Automated release: case confidence 0.55 meets the calibrated gate threshold 0.55.
Key findings: ncr_present present (p=0.81); laterality bilateral (p=0.55).
